transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2025-07-21
- Start: 15:30 PDT
- Duration: ~58 minutes
- Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Luca Romano (Redwood SE), Tess O'Neill (Redwood Solutions), Priya Narang (Omega - Head of Search), Carlos Mendez (Omega - ML Eng), Aisha Khan (Omega - Infra)

Summary:
Technical deep dive covering embedding vector dimensionality, batching and auto-batching strategies, KV/prefix cache behavior in rerank flows, and quantization tradeoffs for both embeddings and cross-encoder rerankers. Customer targets: p95 end-to-end <= 120ms (including network), p99 <= 250ms, steady 500-1000 qps with spikes to 2000 qps. Discussed hosted/dedicated/private deployment options and VPC constraints.

Topics discussed:
- Vector dims impact on latency and cost (64/128/512/1536)
- Batch size, max_batch_latency_ms and adaptive batching
- KV/prefix caching for shared context in rerank flows
- Quantization effects (int8, 4-bit) on accuracy and throughput
- Deployment: VPC peering vs private on-prem, cold starts, warm pools
- Cost modeling per million queries for different dims and deployment modes

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: okay everyone, thanks for hopping on. quick intros and then we'll dig into the numbers Luca ran.
[00:12] Priya Narang: thanks. our main questions are how vector dimension and batching affect the tail latency in our ANN + cross-encoder rerank pipeline. we have a 120ms p95 bar for total request time and a 50ms network budget.
[00:25] Luca Romano: got it. i prepared microbenchmarks on dedicated GPU nodes, i'll summarize verbally and we'll attach the sheet. note: model shorthand like rwd-embed-s/l in the sheet, rwd-embed-l is the 1536-d variant.
[00:38] Carlos Mendez: can you give ballparks for latency and cost deltas per dim? finance wants order-of-magnitude numbers.
[00:44] Maya Chen: we will share a precise cost table, but roughly CPU/GPU compute scales with vector dim (FLOPs) and memory bandwidth; network and storage also scale for uncompressed vectors. compressed/quantized vectors reduce egress.
[00:58] Luca Romano: bench highlights (dedicated cluster):
- 64d embed: p95 ~8ms non-batched; batched 128 -> ~3ms per item.
- 128d embed: p95 ~12ms non-batched; batched 64 -> ~4ms.
- 512d embed: p95 ~38ms non-batched; batched 32 -> ~12-14ms.
- 1536d embed: p95 ~120ms non-batched; batched 8 -> ~40-45ms.
(These are embed-only forward times, not including ANN fetch or rerank).
[01:45] Aisha Khan: 45ms for 1536 dims is pretty tight given our 50ms network budget.
[01:49] Luca Romano: right. for high-dim you'd typically do hybrid: index with 512d vectors for ANN, keep 1536d for offline or optional higher-quality checks, or quantize the large vectors. alternatively, smaller cross-encoder models for rerank help.
[02:05] Tess O'Neill: our auto-batching engine will try to merge requests but you can cap max_batch_latency_ms to meet SLOs; typical values for low-latency are 8-12ms. that setting plus max_batch_size controls the latency/throughput point.
[02:20] Priya Narang: what about KV cache? our flow is: user query -> embed -> ANN -> top-30 -> cross-encoder rerank with concatenated candidate contexts. where does caching help?
[02:33] Luca Romano: KV cache is most effective for autoregressive generation where there's incremental decoding. for cross-encoders (single forward pass) you can still cache repeated static prefixes or candidate encodings. if candidates share a common large prefix (e.g., product description), you can cache its activations and avoid recompute. that can cut rerank compute by ~30-60% depending on prefix size.
[02:56] Carlos Mendez: our ANN pipeline uses FAISS on the VPC. do you recommend pulling compressed vectors into the rerank pod or streaming raw candidate text? network cost is a concern.
[03:07] Luca Romano: common pattern: ANN on your FAISS, return top-k ids, fetch compressed vectors + metadata, run a cheap vector-based rescoring inline, and only call the heavy cross-encoder for top-30. compressed int8 vectors save 30-60% egress. we'll model the numbers once we have your top-k sizes and qps.
[03:27] Aisha Khan: we will not allow public internet egress for model weights. can Redwood run in our VPC or do we need private deployment?
[03:35] Maya Chen: you can run Redwood Private inside your VPC (customer-managed control plane) or use Dedicated with VPC peering. Private is required for strict air-gapped setups. we'll share the private deployment checklist.
[03:48] Priya Narang: for our latency targets at 1k qps, what concrete config would you suggest to hit p95 120ms and p99 250ms?
[03:59] Luca Romano: plausible config: 512-d embeddings for ANN, target embed batch 16-32 (auto-batcher with 10ms max latency), lightweight inline scoring, cross-encoder quantized to int8 on dedicated capacity for rerank pods, and prefix/candidate caching. with that we see p95 ~90-110ms in our dedicated runs. p99 depends on warm pool size and cold starts.
[04:21] Carlos Mendez: when you say "dedicated capacity" what is that in GPU terms?
[04:25] Luca Romano: for the runs above, think 2x A10 GPUs for sustained 1k qps if cross-encoder is heavy (seq len 256, top-30). if you quantize to 4-bit and/or use a smaller reranker, you can drop to 1x A10 and CPU workers for glue. A100s give more throughput at higher batch sizes, but if you favor small batches A10 can be more cost efficient. we will output a per-GPU throughput/cost table.
[04:50] Priya Narang: how reliable is 4-bit quant on rerank accuracy?
[04:55] Luca Romano: it varies. embeddings often tolerate int8 with <1-2% similarity drop; 4-bit (Q4) can be model-dependent and sometimes introduces noticeable drift. for cross-encoders we recommend int8 first and run calibration/evals on your labeled pairs before moving to Q4. we can run that calibration in 48-72 hours once you provide samples.
[05:14] Carlos Mendez: we have ~20k labeled pairs from offline judge, should be enough.
[05:18] Luca Romano: perfect, that will let us run precision@k and MRR comparisons across dims and quant levels.
[05:25] Tess O'Neill: note that batch sizing interacts with quantization benefits: larger batches show more throughput uplift from int8/4-bit because memory bandwidth and compute get amortized. tiny batches sometimes show smaller speedups.
[05:40] Priya Narang: network sizing question: if we keep FAISS and vectors in our VPC and Redwood runs in the same VPC, what's typical egress per request for top-30 rerank?
[05:50] Luca Romano: payload depends on candidate size and compression. uncompressed top-30 vectors + metadata might be 10-25KB; with int8 compression you can reduce that by ~30-60%. multiply by qps for egress. we'll model this precisely in the followup.
[06:08] Aisha Khan: cold starts are a concern. what warmup times do you see?
[06:12] Luca Romano: depends on model size and weight locality. 512-d embed models from local NVMe: cold start ~3-8s. 1536-d models can be ~8-20s. to avoid user-visible tail spikes we recommend min-replicas / warm pool.
[06:27] Carlos Mendez: do you support async rerank where a fast inline score is returned and final score arrives later?
[06:31] Maya Chen: yes, you can implement staged scoring: cheap embed-based score inline, heavy rerank async with callback or webhook. Redwood supports streaming partial results as well.
[06:40] Priya Narang: observability: we need traces, token-level cost and per-route latency to tie back to billing.
[06:46] Luca Romano: Redwood Console offers token-level cost, per-model traces and per-route dashboards. you can export to your billing system and attach RBAC controls.
[06:54] Tess O'Neill: also, application-level caching of very frequent queries gives big multiplicative savings; our cost optimizer will flag high-value cache candidates.
[07:02] Priya Narang: any on-prem / air-gapped gotchas?
[07:05] Maya Chen: air-gapped means we ship a private package and you run control plane; ops overhead includes patching and image updates. we'll provide a runbook and ports list.
[07:15] Priya Narang: SLA for dedicated?
[07:18] Maya Chen: dedicated is SLA-backed for uptime (typically 99.9%) and latency targets for the reserved pool; contract has detailed terms. fallbacks and canaries are configurable.
[07:28] Carlos Mendez: last ask: can you show a 12-month TCO comparing hosted, dedicated, private for 1k qps with mid/low/high dims and quant levels?
[07:35] Maya Chen: yes, included in next steps. we'll produce sensitivity analysis by dim, batch size and quantization.
